messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Multiple customers reporting 503/timeout errors for EU region over the last 7m. Error spike correlated with DNS resolution failures for eu.redwood.ai (Cloudflare/Route53 geoDNS path). Paging Sam (oncall) and NetOps (Jay).

Sam (oncall): I see the alert. Confirming -- is it just EU or global?

Maria (sre): Metrics: origin healthy, apps responding when hit directly by IP. Failure appears at DNS layer + increased resolver errors from EU resolvers (timeouts, SERVFAIL).

Jay (netops): We're seeing anomalous AS paths to Cloudflare edges in eu-west-1 region, and Route53 health checks are fine. Looks like Cloudflare AS-level filtering causing some resolver failures. Traceroute from eu probe: 
```
traceroute to eu.redwood.ai (104.18.23.45), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.0.1  0.5 ms  0.4 ms  0.4 ms
 2  * * *
 3  52.95.12.9  12.3 ms  12.2 ms  12.1 ms
 4  104.18.23.45  45.2 ms  45.1 ms  45.0 ms
```
But dig shows intermittent SERVFAIL: 
```
$ dig +short @1.1.1.1 eu.redwood.ai A
; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```

Anna (oncall): I'm taking the pager from Sam in 5m; Sam can you brief me on mitigations tried?

Sam (oncall): Brief: restarted local DNS cache on edge proxies (no effect), validated origin health, opened ticket with Cloudflare (ref #CF-9281). Trying immediate mitigation: switch geoDNS fallback to secondary provider and lower TTLs.

deploy-bot: Scheduled change: update Route53 failover traffic policy -> attach secondary pool (backup-dns) at 1717554700. Requires manual confirmation: `yes`/`no`.

Sam (oncall): I approve. deploy-bot, proceed.

Jay (netops): I'll push Cloudflare worker-level redirect as additional fail-safe for EU. Also initiating BGP path refresh with partner.

Maria (sre): Adding diagnostic commands for anyone joining:
```
# quick checks
dig +nocmd eu.redwood.ai A @1.1.1.1 +noall +answer
curl -sS --resolve "eu.redwood.ai:443:104.18.23.45" https://eu.redwood.ai/health || true
```

Eli (cs): Field reports: 5 enterprise customers reporting UI timeouts; one started rolling back features. We should update status page and set expectation: ongoing DNS issue impacting EU routing.

Sam (oncall): Route53 policy applied at 1717554700. Confirming TTL changed from 300 -> 60 on eu.redwood.ai to speed failover propagation.

incident-bot: CHANGELOG: Route53 traffic policy updated by Sam (oncall) at 1717554700.

Jay (netops): Confirming partial recovery: many EU resolvers now resolve to secondary pool IPs (backup-dns) but a subset of resolvers still get stale Cloudflare records due to upstream resolver caches. Propagation estimate: up to 5m for 60s TTL + some stale caches.

Anna (oncall): I'm taking over the page now from Sam. Action items: 1) Keep TTL at 60 for 30m, 2) continue Cloudflare escalation, 3) notify customers with highest impact. Sam, handing off logs and ticket refs to me.

Sam (oncall): Handing off. Ticket refs: CF-9281, AWS-14322. Logs: /var/log/edges/dns_cache_eu.log (last 1h attached in ops).

Eli (cs): Sending targeted DM to top-10 customers in EU about mitigation steps and ETA. Will post a public status update: "Investigating: DNS resolution issues impacting EU routing. Mitigation in progress."

Maria (sre): Additional mitigation: enabling HTTP-level fallback for API route to accept requests on global hostname with header `X-Region: eu` for affected customers. Applying canary now.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for header-fallback route at 1717555200 -> 10% traffic to fallback.

Jay (netops): Cloudflare support answered: confirmed partial outage on select EU PoPs, engineering engaged. They recommended our secondary pool as a mitigation and suggested keeping TTL low.

Anna (oncall): Monitoring: error rate dropped from 18% -> 4% in 12m after failover. Still seeing isolated resolver timeouts (likely ISP caches). Next steps: keep TTL low for 1hr, confirm no data loss, and prepare rollback plan.

Eli (cs): Status page updated at 1717555400. Customers notified. No escalations yet.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: geo-dns-cloudflare-eu | status: mitigation_in_progress | severity: P2 | start_ts: 1717554321

Anna (oncall): If anyone sees a customer with persistent issues, DM me directly. I'm staying on until full recovery and official postmortem assignment. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

Sam (oncall): Thanks everyone — keeping an eye on Cloudflare ticket and will join postmortem.

Maria (sre): Saving timeline and commands to incident folder: /incidents/2024-05-XX-geo-dns-eu. We'll assign postmortem owners after stabilization.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity downgraded to P3 at 1717555789; continued monitoring.
